## Who are you and what business did you start?

Hello! I'm Umair Quarishi, founder of Writegenic AI, an AI-powered platform that simplifies content creation and project documentation for professionals, teams, and SaaS businesses. Our primary customers are content marketers, project managers, and startups looking to save time and boost productivity. What makes WriteGenic.ai special is its ability to generate high-quality, structured documents—from blog posts to business plans—in minutes, not hours. Today, we’re bringing in around $5K/month and growing steadily as more teams discover the power of smart automation.

_

My image

_

## How do you come up with the idea for Writegenic AI ?

The idea for WriteGenic.ai came from a recurring pain point I experienced—spending hours creating structured content, business documents, and project plans while juggling multiple tools. The “aha” moment came during a client project where generating a simple proposal took more time than the actual strategy. I knew there had to be a smarter way. Unlike my earlier ideas, this one solved a clear, repeatable problem for marketers, founders, and project managers. My background in content strategy and SaaS growth gave me insight into what busy professionals actually need—speed, quality, and structure. I started with a basic prototype to automate outline generation and tested it with a small network of users. Their feedback was overwhelmingly positive, validating that people wanted a tool that could do more than just write—it had to think structurally. That’s how WriteGenic.ai was born.

## How did you launch Writegenic AI  and get initial traction?

I launched WriteGenic.ai quietly with a simple landing page and a few demos shared on LinkedIn and in Slack communities for marketers and startup founders. I focused on one message: “Structured content in minutes, not hours.” I didn’t have a huge ad budget, so I relied on early outreach, word-of-mouth, and cold DMs offering free trials in exchange for feedback. The response was surprisingly enthusiastic. People said, “This saves me hours,” and “I wish I had this for my last pitch deck.” The first sale came within two weeks—a small SaaS team paid for a quarterly subscription after trying it for just one day. That moment was unforgettable. It proved that the idea had real value. One key lesson from the launch: don’t wait for perfect. Just launch. I learned that early users don’t expect perfection—they want utility and responsiveness. If I were to do it again, I’d start even leaner and build tighter feedback loops from day one.

## What was the growth strategy for Writegenic AI  and how did you scale?

We’ve grown WriteGenic.ai primarily through organic SEO, content marketing, and community engagement. Since our platform helps users create high-quality content faster, it only made sense to lead by example. I published SEO-optimized blog posts targeting long-tail keywords like “AI project documentation tool” and “how to write a project proposal quickly.” Within three months, we started ranking for competitive terms.

In parallel, I focused heavily on Reddit and LinkedIn. I didn’t sell—just shared tips, templates, and early feature demos. In one case, a Reddit post in r/marketingtools showcasing a real before/after project proposal generated 1,200+ site visits in two days and converted into 30+ trial signups. That strategy worked because it offered real value upfront without being salesy.

Another powerful tactic was partnering with micro-creators on Twitter and niche newsletters. A single mention in a SaaS-focused Substack led to a 9% bump in monthly revenue.

For entrepreneurs just starting out: start small, be useful, and listen like crazy. Every growth channel begins with trust and consistency. You don’t need to be everywhere just be relevant where it matters.

## What were the biggest lessons learned from building Writegenic AI ?

Starting WriteGenic.ai came from my frustration with time-consuming content creation and project documentation. I realized others faced the same issue wasting hours structuring documents when they needed speed and clarity. My background in SaaS and content strategy helped shape a solution powered by AI that actually thinks in templates and outcomes. I validated the idea with early users who loved the speed and structure. That “aha” moment came when a user told me it saved them an entire day of work. From there, I knew this wasn’t just useful it was necessary.
